title: VPC endpoints and PrivateLink: reaching a service without the internet

videos.script: The shop's private machines reach S3 every night, and every byte goes through a NAT gateway. {{nat}} At nine cents a gigabyte, the backups alone cost ninety-five dollars a month, for traffic that never needed the internet. {{endpoints}} A VPC endpoint is the way to an AWS service that stays off the internet. There are two kinds. {{gateway}} A gateway endpoint is a line in a route table. It exists only for S3 and DynamoDB, and it is free. {{interface}} An interface endpoint is a network interface in your own subnet, with a private address. The service's usual name resolves to it, so the application does not change. It is charged by the hour and by the gigabyte. {{policy}} Both can carry a policy, and a bucket can refuse every request that did not come through one. {{privatelink}} Then the same idea, turned around. The shop publishes a service of its own, and another account reaches it through an endpoint. No route joins the two networks. {{end}} By the end you can say which endpoint fits, and what it saves against the NAT gateway of lesson seventeen.
